name: DeepCAD
description: DeepCAD is the seminal deep generative model of CAD command sequences (sketch + extrude operations), released at ICCV 2021. It learns a Transformer-based encoder/decoder over a vocabulary of CAD commands extracted from the ABC dataset (~178k models), enabling unconditional generation of valid parametric CAD programs. The model produces sequences that can be executed in a CAD kernel to recover B-rep geometry, demonstrating that the parametric program — not the resulting mesh — is the right learnable representation for engineering CAD. DeepCAD established the dataset preprocessing pipeline that most subsequent neural-CAD papers (SkexGen, ComplexGen, BRepGen, CAD-MLLM) reuse.

name: SkexGen
organization: Autodesk Research / Simon Fraser University (Xu, Willis, et al.)
description: SkexGen extends DeepCAD's autoregressive program-CAD paradigm with a hierarchical transformer that decomposes generation into separate codebooks for sketch topology, sketch geometry, and extrusion parameters. Trained on the Fusion 360 Gallery sketch-extrude dataset, it generates more diverse and structurally valid CAD programs than DeepCAD, with measurable improvements in JSD/MMD geometric quality metrics. SkexGen's hierarchical decomposition has become a template for subsequent program-CAD generators: factor the design into discrete sub-decisions and learn a separate transformer over each.

name: CAD-MLLM
description: CAD-MLLM frames CAD generation as a multimodal LLM task: given text descriptions, sketches, or point clouds, produce CAD command sequences. Built on top of an open-weight LLM (typically LLaMA-class), it adapts the model with LoRA on a CAD-program corpus, then is conditioned on multimodal prompts. The approach demonstrates that text-to-CAD does not require a bespoke architecture — a general-purpose LLM with appropriate fine-tuning produces parametric CAD programs that compile and execute. Performance on text-conditional benchmarks improves over earlier text-to-CAD baselines.

name: BRepNet
description: BRepNet is a topology-aware neural network operating directly on Boundary Representation (B-rep) data — the native data format of parametric CAD kernels (Parasolid, ACIS, OpenCascade). Rather than converting to a mesh or point cloud, BRepNet defines convolutional operators over the face-edge-vertex graph of the B-rep itself, preserving exact geometric and topological information. Released alongside the Fusion 360 Gallery dataset, it became the reference architecture for downstream tasks like feature recognition, manufacturability analysis, and CAD segmentation that require true CAD topology rather than a mesh approximation.

name: UV-Net
description: UV-Net learns representations of CAD B-rep faces by sampling each face's UV parameter domain and applying 2D CNNs over the resulting tensor — a surface-equivariant representation that respects the curvature and parameterization of analytic surfaces. The network combines per-face UV-CNN features with a graph network over the face adjacency to handle the topological structure. UV-Net is widely cited as the reference embedding method for engineering CAD parts and is the input pipeline for many downstream tasks including assembly retrieval, feature recognition, and DfM checking.

name: PolyGen
description: PolyGen is the first transformer-based autoregressive model of 3D meshes — generating vertices and faces sequentially, treating the mesh as a sequence in the same way GPT treats text. Trained on ShapeNet, PolyGen produces clean polygonal meshes (not point clouds or implicit fields) and demonstrated that transformers scale to 3D structure prediction. It remains a methodological reference for any mesh-as-sequence approach, including MeshGPT, MeshAnything, and the program-CAD generators that followed.

name: MeshGPT
description: MeshGPT learns a vector-quantized embedding of triangle-mesh patches, then trains a GPT-style transformer to autoregressively generate triangle sequences. Unlike voxel or implicit-field approaches, MeshGPT directly produces clean polygonal meshes with sharp edges — the form factor designers actually want. Demonstrated on ShapeNet and benchmarks for chair/table/sofa generation. Subsequent work (MeshAnything, EdgeRunner) extends this paradigm to higher-resolution and conditional generation.

name: Point-E
description: Point-E is OpenAI's text-conditional 3D point cloud diffusion model — released open-source. It uses a two-stage pipeline: a text-to-image diffusion model produces a single rendered view, then a point-cloud diffusion model conditioned on that image produces a 3D point cloud. While the resulting point clouds are sparse (~4k points) and not directly engineering-grade, Point-E was the first widely accessible text-to-3D system and seeded a generation of follow-up work (Shap-E, GET3D, DreamFusion, Magic3D).

name: Shap-E
description: Shap-E is OpenAI's successor to Point-E, generating implicit-function (NeRF or signed distance field) representations rather than point clouds — yielding watertight, textured 3D meshes via marching-cubes extraction. It uses a conditional diffusion model over the parameters of the implicit function. Shap-E's outputs are cleaner than Point-E's but still not engineering-CAD grade. The model is open-source and remains a common baseline for academic text-to-3D research.

name: GET3D
description: GET3D is NVIDIA's GAN-based 3D shape generator that produces textured mesh assets directly — bypassing the slow score-distillation route used by DreamFusion. Built on EG3D's tri-plane representation and DMTet for differentiable mesh extraction, GET3D outputs production-ready textured meshes. It is widely used in graphics and gaming pipelines and has been adapted for engineering contexts, though its outputs are not topologically clean enough for parametric CAD.

name: DreamFusion
description: DreamFusion introduced Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) — a method to lift a 2D text-to-image diffusion model into 3D by optimizing a NeRF whose rendered views match what the 2D diffusion model 'expects' for the prompt. No 3D training data required. Outputs are NeRFs (later extracted to meshes), and the technique has become the dominant approach for text-to-3D throughout 2023–2024. Engineering use is limited because outputs are stylized rather than CAD-precise, but SDS is now a load-bearing technique across the field.

name: Magic3D
description: Magic3D is NVIDIA's high-resolution text-to-3D system. It improves over DreamFusion via a coarse-to-fine pipeline: first run SDS at low resolution with a hash-grid NeRF (Instant-NGP), then convert to a textured mesh and refine with high-resolution score distillation. Generation time drops from hours to ~40 minutes and visual quality improves substantially. Magic3D set the bar for text-to-3D quality through 2023.

name: TripoSR
description: TripoSR is a feed-forward single-image-to-3D model — produces a textured mesh in under a second on consumer GPUs, no per-instance optimization. Built as a transformer over tri-plane features, trained on Objaverse + curated 3D assets. Released open-source by Stability AI and Tripo3D. Set the bar for fast image-to-3D in 2024 and informed many follow-on commercial offerings (Meshy, Tripo3D itself, Rodin).

name: InstantMesh
description: InstantMesh is a fast image-to-3D mesh generator combining a multi-view diffusion model (Zero123++ class) with a sparse-view large reconstruction model (FlexiCubes for differentiable mesh extraction). Produces high-quality textured meshes in seconds. Key engineering contribution: combining FlexiCubes (which gives editable, topologically clean meshes) with diffusion-based view priors. Open-source under Apache 2.0.

name: Trellis
description: Microsoft's Trellis introduces a unified Structured Latent (SLAT) representation that simultaneously encodes geometry, texture, and structure — enabling image- or text-conditional generation of 3D assets in multiple output formats (Gaussian splats, radiance fields, meshes). Trained on a large filtered subset of Objaverse. Trellis became a top-tier reference for high-quality 3D-gen in late 2024 and is open-source under MIT.

name: Hunyuan3D 2
description: Tencent's Hunyuan3D 2 is a two-stage open-source 3D generation system: a shape diffusion model (Hunyuan3D-DiT) followed by a multi-view texture synthesis network (Hunyuan3D-Paint). Released with weights and a hosted commercial endpoint. Achieves geometry quality competitive with closed commercial systems at the time of release; widely benchmarked in academic image-to-3D papers throughout 2025.

name: Zoo Text-to-CAD
description: Zoo's Text-to-CAD is the most prominent commercial text-to-CAD service in the engineering-focused tier — distinct from generic text-to-3D in that it produces parametric CAD output (KCL, Zoo's text-based CAD scripting language) that opens in their modeling kernel. Zoo's broader bet is that the future of CAD is a text-native modeling kernel (KCL) plus an LLM that emits KCL programs. Funded by Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and others.

name: Adam CAD
description: Adam CAD is a YC-backed text-to-CAD startup focused on parametric mechanical part generation, with chat-style refinement and sketch-based editing. Differentiates from generic 3D-gen by targeting CAD output that opens cleanly in Onshape/Solidworks. Operates as both a standalone web tool and an Onshape plugin (covered in the AI-in-Design-Map cad-copilots page).

name: Spectral Labs SGS-1
description: Spectral Labs' SGS-1 (Spectral Generative System) is a text-to-CAD product positioned as the parametric-CAD engine for their CDS 2.0 platform. SGS-1 generates editable parametric features in standard CAD format. Spectral Labs frames the product within a broader generative engineering platform that also covers manufacturability and simulation. Notable for explicitly targeting industrial/engineering teams rather than the prosumer 3D-gen market.

name: Common Sense Machines (CSM)
description: Common Sense Machines (CSM) provides image- and text-to-3D APIs targeted at game developers, e-commerce, and industrial design. Outputs textured meshes with controllable topology. CSM has positioned itself in both the prosumer 3D-gen tier (competing with Meshy, Tripo3D) and the more bespoke industrial tier via their cube-based reconstruction service.

name: Meshy
description: Meshy is a leading prosumer/B2B text-to-3D and image-to-3D platform, competitive with Tripo3D and Rodin. Outputs textured meshes in PBR formats; integrates into Blender, Unity, Unreal pipelines. Meshy is squarely in the asset-generation market — not engineering CAD — but is referenced in engineering contexts as the upstream model class that text-to-CAD borrows architecture from.

name: Tripo3D
description: Tripo3D (the commercial product behind the open-source TripoSR research) is a text/image-to-3D platform with one of the strongest geometry and texture quality scores in the prosumer tier as of 2024-2025. Outputs are PBR-textured meshes; integrates with major DCC tools. Like Meshy, Tripo3D is asset-gen rather than engineering CAD, but the underlying transformer architecture is shared with engineering 3D-gen research.

name: Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)
description: The Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) is the most influential neural operator architecture for learning solution operators of PDEs. By parameterizing convolutional kernels in Fourier space, FNO becomes resolution-invariant and handles a class of PDEs (Navier-Stokes, Darcy flow, Burgers) with order-of-magnitude speedup over classical solvers. Published at ICLR 2021. FNO and its descendants (F-FNO, U-FNO, GINO, PINO) underpin most modern physics-surrogate products including SimScale's Foundation AI Model and Luminary Cloud's SHIFT-Wing.

name: DeepONet
description: DeepONet, by Lu, Jin, and Karniadakis, was the first neural operator architecture with a universal approximation guarantee for nonlinear operators between function spaces. It uses a branch network (encodes input function) and a trunk network (encodes output spatial coordinate), combined as a dot product. DeepONet runs alongside FNO as the canonical operator-learning framework; PI-DeepONet extends it with physics-informed losses, and DeepONet variants underlie multiple production CAE products.

name: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator (GINO)
description: GINO extends FNO to large-scale 3D PDE problems on irregular domains by combining geometric encoders (signed distance fields) with Fourier operators. Demonstrated 26,000× speedup on vehicle aerodynamics. GINO is the architecture underpinning NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo's flagship demonstrations, SimScale's pump foundation model, and Luminary Cloud's SHIFT-Wing — making it the practical reference architecture for production engineering surrogates as of 2024-2026.

name: Physics-Informed Neural Operator (PINO)
description: PINO combines the FNO architecture with physics-informed losses (PDE residuals on the operator output), bridging the data-driven neural-operator paradigm with the constraint-based PINN paradigm. The result is operator learning that requires less labeled data and generalizes better outside training distributions. Frequently cited as the synthesis of the two main scientific-ML schools.

name: MeshGraphNets
description: DeepMind's MeshGraphNets learn mesh-based simulation by message-passing on the simulation graph: nodes are mesh vertices, edges are connectivity, and the network predicts per-node updates per timestep. Demonstrated across cloth, fluids, and structural mechanics. The architecture handles unstructured meshes natively and is the canonical GNN-based surrogate for engineering simulation. Foundational for subsequent work like NVIDIA's MeshGraphNet implementations and Apple's Material-Point GNN models.

name: GraphCast
description: GraphCast is DeepMind's neural weather forecasting model — a graph neural network on a hierarchical icosahedral mesh that produces 10-day global weather forecasts at 0.25° resolution in under a minute, beating the operational ECMWF IFS system on most metrics. Published in Science in 2023. While not engineering CAE, GraphCast is the proof-of-concept that physics foundation models can outperform validated numerical solvers — the benchmark that engineering surrogates are now measured against.

name: FourCastNet
description: FourCastNet is the first FNO-based weather forecasting model to match operational systems on key variables, with 45,000× speedup over IFS. Built on the Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNO). Released open-source via NVIDIA Modulus and remains a reference baseline alongside GraphCast and Pangu-Weather. Demonstrated that operator-learning architectures (FNO family) compete with graph-network architectures (GraphCast) at planetary scale.

name: Aurora
description: Aurora is Microsoft's 1.3B-parameter foundation model for Earth system forecasting — the most rigorous published proof that the foundation-model paradigm works for physics at production scale. Trained on >1M hours of diverse atmospheric/oceanographic data. Outperforms specialized operational models for air quality, ocean waves, tropical cyclone tracks, and high-resolution weather at ~5,000× lower compute cost than IFS. Published in Nature 2025. The benchmark engineering CAE foundation models are now aiming for.

name: Neural Concept Shape
description: Neural Concept Shape is the most established commercial neural-network surrogate for engineering CAE — based on the founder's PhD work on geodesic convolutional networks for 3D shape regression. Used by automotive (Renault, Ferrari), aerospace, and energy customers to predict CFD/structural outputs from 3D geometry in seconds rather than hours. Trained on customer simulation data. Frequently the case-study reference for narrow-surrogate vs foundation-model debates in the surrogate-models school.

name: Monolith AI
description: Monolith AI is a London-based engineering-data ML platform — used by Honda, BMW, Jota Sport, and Honeywell to build custom surrogate models from a customer's existing test/simulation data. Differentiates from neural-operator startups by emphasizing the data-engineering and workflow side: ingest mixed CSV/sensor/simulation data, train tailored ML models, deploy as live surrogates inside the customer's PLM. Strong in motorsport, aerospace, and industrial test-rig replacement.

name: BeyondMath
description: BeyondMath ($18.5M seed) claims to have built the first foundation AI model trained on first-principles physics rather than simulation outputs. Targets real-time engineering simulation at 1,000× speedup. Customer engagements include an F1 team and a $19M Honeywell aerospace project (STRATA). The most aggressive version of the foundation-model thesis: pretraining signal is physics laws, not labeled data. Certification path is the major open question.

name: Luminary Cloud SHIFT-Wing
description: SHIFT-Wing is a transonic aerodynamic foundation model trained on 2,276 high-fidelity adapted-mesh CFD simulations of NASA Common Research Model wing-body geometry (Boeing 777-class). Built with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo's DoMINO architecture; covers Mach 0.5–0.85 and off-design shock interactions. Released open-source for non-commercial use with the dataset on Hugging Face. One of the cleanest reproducible examples of a domain-specific physics foundation model.

name: SimScale AI Foundation Model for Pump Simulation
description: SimScale's pump foundation model (March 2025) is the first production-deployed engineering foundation model — trained on thousands of validated CFD simulations of centrifugal pumps. Delivers 2,700× speedup over traditional solvers; evaluates 60+ pump designs in under 60 seconds. Customers can fine-tune it on proprietary pump datasets. Built on NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. Concrete proof that the foundation-model-for-physics paradigm can ship in CAE.

name: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo (Modulus)
description: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo (formerly Modulus) is the dominant open-source framework for physics-informed neural networks and operator learning. Ships FNO, GINO, DoMINO, MeshGraphNet, and diffusion components; integrates with Omniverse for visualization. Most production physics foundation models (SimScale, Luminary, BeyondMath partners, dozens of NVIDIA Inception startups) are built on PhysicsNeMo. NVIDIA's strategy: be the infrastructure layer beneath every domain-specific model.

name: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN)
description: The original PINN paper (Raissi, Perdikaris, Karniadakis, JCP 2019) defined the modern field of physics-informed deep learning: neural networks trained with PDE residuals as soft constraints, enabling solution of forward and inverse problems with sparse data. Tens of thousands of citations; spawned the entire scientific-ML field including DeepXDE, NVIDIA Modulus, and dozens of variants (VPINN, XPINN, fPINN, BC-PINN). Karniadakis at Brown is the citation epicenter.

name: DeepXDE
description: DeepXDE is the most-used open-source library for PINNs and DeepONet — supports forward/inverse problems for ODEs, PDEs, fractional PDEs, integro-differential equations on TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, and PaddlePaddle backends. Maintained by Lu Lu's group. The reference implementation that academics adopt before considering NVIDIA Modulus or custom code.

name: JAX-MD
description: JAX-MD is Google's differentiable molecular dynamics framework — every step of the simulation is differentiable, enabling gradient-based optimization of materials, forces, and structures. Supports neural network potentials. Underlies a growing fraction of materials-discovery and protein-design pipelines, and is referenced as the differentiable-simulation companion to ML interatomic potentials (NequIP, MACE, Allegro).

name: PhiFlow
description: PhiFlow is Nils Thuerey's group's differentiable fluid simulation library — provides differentiable Navier-Stokes solvers in NumPy / TensorFlow / PyTorch / JAX. Used heavily in Thuerey's group at TU Munich (one of the major academic centers for ML+CFD), and serves as a teaching/research vehicle for differentiable physics. Companion to the Thuerey group's many ML-CFD papers.

name: Warp
description: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for high-performance differentiable simulation on GPUs — used in Omniverse, Isaac Sim, robotics, and computer graphics. Provides differentiable kernels for fluids, solids, granular media, and rigid bodies. Increasingly used for differentiable design pipelines and as the simulation backbone in NVIDIA's robotics + manufacturing demos.

name: TopologyGAN
description: TopologyGAN demonstrated that conditional GANs can predict topology-optimization solutions directly from boundary-condition / load specifications — bypassing the iterative SIMP solver. Trained on 80,000+ TopOpt outputs across diverse load cases. Achieves order-of-magnitude speedup at near-baseline compliance. The reference example for ML-as-fast-surrogate-for-classical-TO, which subsequently spawned DeepTOP, TONR, and many follow-up papers.

name: nTop (nTopology)
description: nTop (formerly nTopology) is the leading commercial implicit-modeling platform for engineering design — used heavily in aerospace, defense, and medical for lattice structures, conformal heat-exchangers, and multi-objective generative design. Distinguishes from Hyperganic by being a programmable graph-based authoring tool rather than an autonomous generator; recently has integrated AI/ML features. Hosts the nCDS (nTop Conformal Design Summit) annually.

name: Hyperganic
description: Hyperganic Core is a Munich-based algorithmic-engineering platform that treats geometry as code: every part is generated by a Python program, enabling extreme parametric/algorithmic complexity (lattice structures, biomimetic geometry, generative parts for AM). Used in aerospace, defense, and rocketry (e.g. Hyperganic + Aleph engine for AM rocket parts). Funded by founders Lin Kayser; Series-A from Earlybird, Vsquared, Eclipse Ventures.

name: Diabatix
description: Diabatix runs ColdStream, a generative-design platform specifically for thermal management (heat sinks, cold plates, electronics cooling). Combines topology-optimization-style generative geometry with CFD-based thermal simulation to produce manufacturable cooling parts in hours. Customer base spans automotive, aerospace, electronics. One of the cleanest examples of a vertical generative-engineering platform.

name: ParaMatters CogniCAD
description: ParaMatters CogniCAD is a generative structural-design platform that automatically produces optimized, manufacturable parts from specified loads, supports, and constraints. Targets automotive and aerospace. Partnered with major OEMs including GM and Lockheed Martin. Distinguishes from raw TopOpt by automating the post-processing back to clean CAD geometry.

name: Synera (formerly Elise)
description: Synera (rebranded from Elise GmbH in 2023) is a German low-code platform for parametric/generative engineering — connects CAD, simulation, optimization, and manufacturing in a node-graph workflow. Customers include automotive and industrial OEMs. Differentiates from Hyperganic by emphasizing workflow orchestration over pure algorithmic design.

name: Fusion 360 Generative Design
description: Fusion 360 Generative Design (originally based on Frustum acquisition by PTC, separately built by Autodesk) is the most accessible commercial generative-design tool — included in Fusion 360 subscriptions. Produces multiple manufacturable design candidates from load/constraint specs across multiple manufacturing processes (milling, AM, casting). Volume usage exceeds bespoke generative-design startups simply because it ships in Fusion 360 by default.

name: Altair Inspire
description: Altair Inspire is a long-standing commercial topology-optimization and generative-design tool, derived from Altair's OptiStruct solver — one of the original commercial TopOpt engines. Recent versions integrate AI assistants (Inspire AI). Strong in automotive and heavy-equipment OEMs. The deep solver heritage (OptiStruct) makes it the most-trusted classical TO engine in industry.

name: MatterGen
description: MatterGen (Microsoft Research, Nature 2025) is a diffusion model for inorganic crystal structure generation, conditioned on target properties (chemistry, symmetry, magnetic, electronic, mechanical). Trained on Materials Project + Alexandria; predictions verified by DFT and experimental synthesis at PNNL. Released open-source. The reference generative-materials model alongside DeepMind's GNoME.

name: GNoME
description: GNoME (Graph Networks for Materials Exploration) by DeepMind discovered 2.2M new stable inorganic crystals — a 10× expansion of the known stable-materials universe. Combines graph neural networks for property prediction with active learning. Published in Nature 2023. Triggered an industry-wide push toward generative-materials platforms (MatterGen, MatterSim) and active-learning labs (A-Lab Berkeley).

name: DiffCSP
description: DiffCSP is a diffusion model for crystal structure prediction that respects crystallographic equivariances (translation, rotation, periodic boundary). Achieved state-of-the-art on the Carbon-24 and Perov-5 benchmarks at NeurIPS 2023. Architecturally distinct from MatterGen by using fractional coordinates and a periodic-equivariant network. Frequently cited as the best academic-only baseline for generative crystal modeling.

name: MACE
description: MACE is a higher-order equivariant message-passing neural network for ML interatomic potentials — combines the higher-body-order expansion of ACE (Atomic Cluster Expansion) with E(3)-equivariant network design. Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and stability on materials and molecular benchmarks; underlies several large-scale materials-foundation-model efforts. Open-source under MIT.

name: NequIP
description: NequIP introduced rotationally-equivariant graph neural networks (E(3)NN) for ML interatomic potentials — yielded order-of-magnitude data efficiency improvements over invariant baselines. Extensively used in catalysis (Open Catalyst Project), materials, and chemistry. Published in Nature Communications 2022; foundation for the Allegro and MACE follow-ons.

name: Allegro
description: Allegro is a strictly local, equivariant interatomic potential — a follow-on from NequIP from the Kozinsky lab. Locality enables linear scaling to large systems (millions of atoms) without sacrificing accuracy. Demonstrated on water, electrolytes, and metal-organic frameworks. Reference architecture for production-scale MLIP deployments.

name: M3GNet
description: M3GNet is a graph neural network ML potential trained on the Materials Project relaxation trajectories — a universal interatomic potential covering 89 elements. Used to relax candidate structures at scale (e.g. in GNoME's pipeline) without per-system DFT. The most-cited universal ML potential alongside CHGNet.

name: CHGNet
description: CHGNet (Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network) is a universal interatomic potential from the Ceder group at Berkeley — uniquely incorporates magnetic moments and charge states, enabling accurate energy/force prediction for transition-metal oxides and battery cathode materials. Trained on Materials Project trajectories. Reference baseline for battery and energy-materials applications.

name: ABC: A Big CAD Model Dataset
description: The ABC dataset (Koch et al., CVPR 2019) is a collection of 1M+ CAD models in STEP/B-rep/mesh formats, scraped from Onshape's public model library. The default training set for nearly every B-rep-learning paper (DeepCAD, BRepNet, UV-Net, BRepGen). Without ABC, the field of neural CAD reconstruction would not exist in its current form.

name: Fusion 360 Gallery Dataset
description: Fusion 360 Gallery is Autodesk's curated dataset of CAD construction sequences — sketch-and-extrude programs with full feature history, not just the final B-rep. Critical for program-CAD generation research (SkexGen, BRepGen, JoinABLE) because it preserves the procedural knowledge that ABC lacks. The standard benchmark for sketch-extrude program generation.

name: Onshape Aikido (CoPilot)
description: Onshape's AI features, internally named Aikido / CoPilot, surface inside Onshape's cloud-native CAD UI — providing natural-language model search, sketch suggestions, and feature recommendations. Distinguishes from desktop CAD AI by leveraging Onshape's cloud architecture for fleet-wide learning across all customer documents (with consent). Launched 2024, expanding through 2025.

name: Autodesk Project Bernini
description: Project Bernini is Autodesk's research foundation model for 3D shape generation — explicitly positioned as Autodesk's bet on a future where generative 3D becomes the input layer to Fusion 360 / Maya / Inventor. Trained on a curated dataset of CAD and design assets. Released as a research preview in 2024 with the explicit goal of integrating into production CAD/M&E products over time.

name: Ansys Discovery + AI+
description: Ansys Discovery integrates real-time GPU-accelerated solvers with AI-assisted simulation setup; the broader Ansys AI+ initiative adds generative-AI assistants and ML surrogates across the Ansys product line (Mechanical, Fluent, HFSS). Among the largest commercial CAE vendors integrating AI throughout the workflow rather than as a standalone product.

name: aPriori AI
description: aPriori is the long-established commercial platform for digital manufacturing simulation and cost analysis — recently augmented with AI features (aPriori AI) for design-for-cost analysis, manufacturability checking, and supplier quoting. Used by Fortune 500 manufacturers to estimate part cost and DFM violations directly from CAD. The reference incumbent in the rule-first DfM space, now adding ML.

name: DFMPro
description: DFMPro by HCLTech is a long-running CAD plugin (Solidworks, NX, Creo) that runs hundreds of rule-based DfM checks across machining, sheet metal, casting, injection molding, and AM processes — increasingly augmented with ML on customer-specific rule learning. Reference example of the rule-first DfM school, now layering ML.

name: Castor Technologies
description: Castor is an Israeli startup providing automated AM-screening — given a CAD assembly, identifies which parts are economically and technically suitable for 3D printing across metal, polymer, and composite processes. Combines rule-based DfAM checks with ML-based cost prediction. Used by major OEMs to qualify AM use cases at scale.

name: Xometry Instant Quoting Engine
description: Xometry's Instant Quoting Engine uses ML on millions of parts and quotes to deliver real-time price estimates for CNC, sheet metal, injection molding, and 3D printing parts directly from uploaded CAD. The reference example of ML-based manufacturing quoting at scale; competitors include Protolabs, Plethora, Fictiv, and Hubs.

name: Markforged Eiger AI
description: Markforged's Eiger software now ships AI features (Blacksmith, AI build orientation, in-process quality monitoring via the X7 printer's vision system). One of the production-deployed examples of ML for AM process monitoring + DfAM in the prosumer/industrial-AM tier.

name: Carbon Design Engine
description: Carbon's Design Engine is a parametric/generative tool tightly integrated with Carbon's resin-based AM process — used heavily for cushioning lattices (Adidas 4DFWD soles, Riddell helmet pads) and biomedical lattices. One of the most production-deployed examples of generative lattice design at scale (millions of parts shipped).
